identity.author: Perpetua, Saturus, and the Redactor
identity.edition: Gebhardt, Acta martyrum selecta (1902), Passio SS. Perpetuae et Felicitatis

sections.locus: Gebhardt VII.XVII (the free supper; Saturus's warning)
source_text: Pridie quoque cum illam caenam ultimam, quam liberam uocant, quantum in ipsis erat non caenam liberam sed agapen caenarent, eadem constantia ad populum uerba iactabant, comminantes iudicium dei, contestantes passionis suae felicitatem, inridentes concurrentium curiositatem, dicente Saturo: Crastinus uobis satis non est, quod libenter uidetis quos odistis? Hodie amici, cras inimici? Notate tamen uobis facies nostras diligenter, ut recognoscatis nos in die illo. Ita omnes inde adtoniti discedebant: ex quibus multi crediderunt.
english: On the day before as well, when they ate that final meal which is called the free one, so far as it lay with them they ate it not as a free feast but as an agape, and with the same steadfastness they hurled words at the people, threatening the judgment of God, bearing witness to the blessedness of their suffering, and laughing to scorn the curiosity of those who flocked together, while Saturus said: Is tomorrow not enough for you, that you willingly gaze upon those whom you hate? Friends today, enemies tomorrow? Yet mark our faces well for yourselves, so that you may know us again on that day.
So they all left that place stunned, and many of them believed.
